properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/29/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/29/2025
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8242705
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2025
Comments: On July 29, 2025, the DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of EQTs Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 7/28/2025 at 2:54 pm.The spill report stated that at 2:06 pm on 7/28/2025, over 5 gallons of production fluids were found on the gravel well pad at the Porter Well site after removing secondary containment. Accompanying during today's inspection is EQTs representative Kyle Borden.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 Sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had different Operator information on it than the Act 9 sign. The DEP recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. At the time of this inspection, drill outs were recently completed on the 6U and containment was removed from the well pad the day prior. Mr. Borden stated that the secondary containment in the release area was packed with tanks and large equipment, therefore despite routine inspections of the containment, only the edges of the containment could be inspected, and no holes or tears were observed. However, upon removal of the containment, staining and small puddles were observed on the gravel pad in an approximately 115 ft x 60 ft area. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to wellheads covered by boxes. The pea gravel in this area was observed to be wet with sections that appeared to be darker in color than other areas. Mr. Borden stated that SPSI and Moody were arriving on site to remediate the release and that they estimate remediation to be completed within the day. EQT representative Schuyler Brounce mentioned in his email (documented in IR 4024285), that following his review of the incident, he estimates the release to be over 1 barrel. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Borden stated once all contaminated gravel has been removed, an updated quantity will be provided to the DEP.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected soil readings of 1.835 mS, 3.22 mS, 3.35 mS and 2.08 mS in the incident area closest to the wellheads, as well as 2.56 mS between two wellheads and a fluid reading of Over Range in fluid observed to be pooled in secondary containment adjacent to the release area. These conductivity readings are elevated when compared to the background soil reading of 0.1457 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign.At the time of this inspection, the DEP requested secondary containment logs for the Porter well pad and Mr. Borden stated they would be provided to the Department electronically. The DEP is also requesting an electronic copy of the Safety Data Sheets for all chemicals stored/utilized within and near the secondary containment that was observed to have the release underneath by COB 8/5/2025.The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the over 1 barrel release of production fluids on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/17/2024 to PENNECO OIL CO INC in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland county. CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNECO OIL CO INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/17/2024
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8184479
Permit API: 129-28783
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 4/17/2024
Comments: This is an Admin inspection report documenting the receipt of the analytical results (attached to this report) from the aqueous samples collected during the time of IR 3742855 from the onsite unnamed stream/tributary on 4/08/2024. The final analytical sample result was received on 4/17/2024.In Sample 9560 - 367 (UV/IR) which was collected at the Potential Point of Impact in response to an observed film/sheen, the UV analysis detected a petroleum product in this sample and suggested that it was crude oil. This corroborates with the onsite unnamed stream/tributary being impacted by the spill that occurred onsite the day prior to collection of these samples, as oil was released during this spill according to the report that was submitted when it occurred.No petroleum products were detected in the aqueous samples collected upstream and downstream of this Potential Point of Impact. The remaining analytical sample results collected at the Potential Point of Impact appeared to be comparable with those collected upstream and downstream. This suggests that brine and/or other pollutants were not released into this unnamed stream/tributary, and that the oil released into this unnamed stream/tributary appeared to be contained to the Potential Point of Impact. Based upon review of these analytical sample results, additional violations are being issued as the Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted by the 4/07/2024 oil spill.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 954576
Permit API: 063-33347
Unconventional: Yes
County: Indiana
Municipality: Grant Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/06/2022
Comments: On 5/6/22 at 1050 hrs., I conducted a routine inspection of Diversified Production, LLC's Leonard Mumau 2 well (API 063-33347) in Grant Twp., Indiana County. The well is a vertical Marcellus well, drilled in 2003. A brine tank located onsite appears to be structurally sound. The well is equipped for production. A site ID sign is posted. A permanent well tag is not affixed to the well head. A violation of OGA 3211(H) is cited for this inspection. There is no active ESCGP for the site. The well pad is restored and permanently stabilized; however, the access road is not stabilized and shows evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation along the entire length of the road. PCSM BMPs have not been maintained along the access road. Sediment laden runoff was observed leaving the access road, crossing Nashville Road, and entering an unnamed tributary of Barrett Run (Ch. 93 designated HQ-CWF). Violations of 102.11(A)2, 78a.53, and CSL 401 are being cited this inspection for failure to implement and maintain PCSM BMPs along the access road and discharging sediment into waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: On April 15th, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill incident reported to the Department for the Gospel Church Unit 10H Well Site in Plum Borough, Allegheny County. The Department reached out to Marc Jacobs of Penneco for additional information on the spill. Per Mr. Jacobs, the well tender discovered the spill on 4/15/2022. The spill occurred at a broken valve on one of the production tanks due to freeze/thaw. They estimate approximately 1 barrel of crude oil has been released and contained within the earthen dike. Cleanup crews have been called to the site. At this time, released oil is being absorbed with pads and peat soil until remediation efforts can continue on Monday. On Monday, 3rd party consultant (Woodard Curran) will be onsite to evaluate release. The affected production tanks will be removed and release area will be remediated. At time of inspection, several Penneco representatives were onsite finishing preliminary clean up efforts. Per Penneco representative, the release was discovered around 10am on 4/15/2022 by the well tender. The spill was estimated to occur sometime between 4/12/2022 (the last visit to the well site) and 4/15/2022. Penneco rep estimated release to be about 1 barrel at the production tank. A vacuum truck was onsite to remove surface crude oil from the release site. Rep stated that on 4/18/2022, two of the three tanks are to be removed and release area to be excavated. Release site was isolated within the dike around the production tanks. Absorbent pads and peat laid within the release area. The broken valve and pipe laid within the dike. There also appeared to be a release at the well head. Per Penneco Rep, there was a release of approximately 5 gallons from around the pump jack. Follow up inspection to be conducted upon completion of remediation efforts. The Department recommends Operator remediate impacted area IAW spill policy for releases greater than 42 gallons. The Department requests the following: disposal records/ manifests for removal of all impacted materials once available, quantity released at the production tank valve and at the well head, how quantity was determined, method of remediation, timeline of when the remediation will be completed, when the release around the wellhead occurred, why the release around the well head occurred and what was released at the well head. Based on today's observations, violations are being issued.

Inspection Date: 7/17/2026
Comments: On 7/17/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection was conducted in response to notification from Seneca of the installation of a concrete catch basin and corrugated pipe on the north side of the pad to capture surface waters on the pad. It was 70 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. I was unaccompanied during the inspection. When I arrived on site, I observed a trench that had recently been dug along the north side of the pad, the trench leading to a 4' x 2' x 2' deep cement catch basin as seen in pictures 12, 13, and 14. I did observe liquid in the trench that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS5 meter. The upper limit of the meter for conductivity is 19.99 mS. The liquid was flowing into the cement catch basin. A vac truck was staged on site with hose ends located in the catch basin, able to remove the accumulating liquids. The fluids were being transferred to a frac tank that had been staged near the catch basin. I inspected the bottom of the center rock lined outfall on the north side of the pad where it leads into the sediment basin. I did not observe liquids discharging from the pad into the basin during this inspection. Liquid in the sediment basin near the northeast overflow field tested at 9.01 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551266 from the sediment basin near the northeast overflow.13 wells have been completed at the site and were staged for flow-back/production. Sand separators and three-phase separators were installed on each of eight recently completed wellheads. The three-phase separators were being used to separate water, gas, and oil. The rig/frac operations secondary containment structure remains installed around the well heads, the sand separators and the three-phase units. Two produced water tanks and 13 GPUs were stationed in secondary containment. Nine frac tanks have been installed in secondary containment south of the eight new gas wells, these being used for flow-back. 32 frac tanks used during fracking operations remain stationed in secondary containment on the west side of the pad.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1030 hours.

Comments: On August 4, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Lamacz #1 well site in Penn Township, Westmoreland County. The inspection was conducted as follow up to a release reported to the Department on 7/19/2021, see inspection #3222750 for previous observations and violations related to the release. At the time of inspection, the impacted material appeared to be excavated and placed under a plastic tarp on the well site. The impacted excavation area appeared to be 30’x60’ and approximately 10’ in depth. The excavation appeared to be following a buried black plastic pipe possibly the gathering pipeline. The excavation of the flow path appeared to be 6" deep, 10’ wide and 500’ in length. The excavation appears to be similar to the impacted location observed on 7/19/2021. The operator has installed temporary ES BMPs and what appear to be oil booms on the excavated flow path. The remediation of spill on the well site has uncovered and damaged what appears to be an encapsulated drill pit or onsite waste disposal location. I observed three sections of the torn black plastic sheeting at different elevation within the excavation. The material contained between the black plastic sheets appeared to be dark gray in color and approximately 2" thick. I recommend that the operator identify the contents of the dark gray material and remediate as needed based on the common constituents/indicators of a release related to brine and cuttings. Violations remain outstanding as they relate to the release on 7/19/2021. Additional violations maybe pending further investigation.

The production chart was labeled 11-29-2023 and showed constant production. During the time of the inspection the 2023 APR/MIA has not been received. No gas was detected in the surrounding soils or on the other equipment. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/17/2024 to GREYLOCK PROD LLC in Hector Township, Potter county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/17/2024
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8211208
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/17/2024
Comments: On 12/17/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 45F and sunny. An Act 9 sign and well permits are visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Hydraulic fracturing activities remain ongoing onsite and are estimated to be completed near the end of next week. Equipment to support well stimulation remain onsite and all equipment which is required to be held in containment was observed in secondary containment structures (photos #2-6)This inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced fluids from secondary containment reported by Greylock on 12/13/2024 at 0245 hours (CTS #385788). The cause of the release was determined to be a hydraulic fracturing pump which leaked produced fluids that accumulated and overtopped from secondary containment; the release has been contained. Contaminated material was already removed and backfilled by my arrival onsite (photo #7). The soil in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at ~40us/cm. Standing fluids were observed near the area of the release and field measured for EC at ~1140us/cm. Two vacuum trucks for removing fluids have been stationed onsite and were sent to remove the fluids from this area. Greylock took corrective action after this release and rebuilt the entire containment berm and rig-matting system with an 18-inch wall for increased capacity and to prevent additional releases (photo #8).The low points of the produced fluids offload containment structure which was the site of the release on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) have been repaired and a pump has been installed to continuously remove fluids from this containment structure as they accumulate (photos #9-11).The drainage system which was conveying fluids and diesel into the site's infiltration basin on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) remains shut in and a pump has been installed to remove accumulating fluids. No fluids were observed entering the basin at the time of this inspection (photo #12). Contaminated materials have not yet been excavated from the basin as per my previous recommendation to follow Act 2 remediation guidelines (photo #13).The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to remove fluids as they accumulate in secondary containment structures.-Continue following Act 2 remediation requirements for the ongoing remediation efforts onsite, including those set to take place in the infiltration basin.-Continuing daily secondary containment inspection.No additional violations noted at this time. The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Meeting on site today with CHK Consultant Brett Fowler. Weather conditions at time of inspection are overcast and 39 degrees F. According to the Emergency Response Notification Report at 1300 hours the following occurred, "up welling of pad adjacent to well head caused concern; Expand started digging at on 11/11/24 at 1:00 p.m.; Expand Energy started digging and encountered produced water with a conductivity of 8000 s/cm. Source of produced water is unknown. Ms. Schaad said that the produced water was not coming up from around the well casing. Expand Energy has Creston Environmental on site utilizing a vac truck to empty excavation. Ms. Schaad said that a small volume of produced water (greater than 5 gallons) has been recovered."At time of inspection, the Department observed a trench dug adjacent to the 5HC well in the affected area. The Department conducted conductivity screenings of the affected area using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Puddled fluid collected in the trench in the affected area was observed with electrical conductivity readings of 3.24 mS/cm. CHK has contracted with Creston Environmental to pursue Act 2 site characterization. According to Mr. Fowler, Nine Energy Services is conducting wireline operations to change out a valve on the 23HC well (API#113-20465). Plugs have been drilled out, but the wells are shut in and no production equipment has yet been set up on this pad. Rig mats are also observed being stacked and removed from the location at time of inspection. A supersucker vacuum truck is observed on site removing high conductivity fluids from the impacted rock stockpiled in the northwest corner of the pad (photo 5). Additional puddles with elevated conductivity readings ranging from 2.2-2.7 mS/cm were observed (photo 6) where impacted pad rock is stockpiled. The Department recommends vacuuming fluid from surface puddles adjacent to the stockpile. During site walk, the Department inspected downslope areas of the well pad to determine if fluid was released from the pad surface. No indication of off-pad release was observed. Violations noted. Violations remain outstanding against API# 113-20470 for SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b) dated 9/23/24.

properties.content:

Permit API: 081-21995
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/30/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite on 6/30/25 in response to a reported release of at least 5 gallons of produced fluid. The release occurred near the evaporator units on the eastern side of the pad and may have been the result of a faulty inlet valve on the evaporators. Tobias Machine and Welding, Penn E and R, and Rick Hall (EQT) were onsite to screen and assess the extent of the release. There were two stains visible on the pad (Photos 1 and 2). The larger stain was approximately 13' by 6' and the smaller stain was approximately 4' by 1'. There was no visible fluid off the pad surface but soil conductivity readings were taken. The soil below the staining between the toe of the pad slope and about halfway to the treeline (Photos 3, 4, and 5) had conductivities over 4.00 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). Closer to the trees the soil conductivity dropped to around 2.2 mS/cm. Inside the woods the conductivity ranged between 0.05 mS/cm to 0.21 mS/cm.I returned on 7/2/25 to check on the progress of the remediation. The impacted area had been scraped (Photos 6, 7, and 8). Soil conductivity was again checked. Conductivities outside the scraped area ranged from 0.20 mS/cm to 0.40 mS/cm. There were a few localized areas within the work area that ranged between 1.74 mS/cm and 3.17 mS/cm. These readings were generally shallow and appeared where there were scrape marks from the excavation. Tobias was going to continue removing soil from these areas as they were finishing the bulk of the remediation. The excavated area was roughly 50' from the pad to the treeline and about 20' to 30' across.During a phone call with Rick Hall (EQT) on 7/3/25, it was determined that the remediated area had been backfilled and stabilized. There were 7 dumpsters of impacted soil that were in the process of being disposed of. EQT also indicated that remediation under Act 2 would be pursued and Penn E and R already collected the necessary confirmation samples.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). The violations may be closed after the completion of Act 2 remediation.
